audit.whatIsWrong: Text credited Xerath with 'passive mana-shield tankiness' in whys[1], spikes[0] and early.
audit.why: Mana Surge only restores mana on basic attacks, with the cooldown reduced on unit kills. Xerath has no shield and no tankiness from his passive. The real early lever is range: Eye of Destruction 1000 and Shocking Orb 1050 against Ahri's 970 Q.
audit.corrected: He pokes from outside your Q because of range and mana sustain, not because he is tanky.
sources: brief enemyKit passive text and ranges

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes named the phases but carried no cooldowns; packet flags zero sequencing cues in the whole matchup.
audit.why: Shocking Orb is 13/12.5/12/11.5/11s and is his only CC; Arcanopulse 9s at rank 1; Rite of the Arcane 130/115/100s.
audit.corrected: Every commit is keyed to the dodged Shocking Orb and its 13-second window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states that Charm cancels Rite of the Arcane, or that Xerath is immobilized for its whole duration.
audit.why: His R carries the channel flag ('interruptible — any CC cancels it') and the description says he immobilizes himself. Charm is hard CC at 975 range, and Spirit Rush closes to it.
audit.corrected: Flank with Spirit Rush and charm him mid-channel — the ultimate ends and he is rooted where you find him.
sources: brief enemyKit R flags and text

audit.whatIsWrong: LEVEL CHART DISAGREEMENT ON ALL SEVEN ROWS: phases[].side read Xerath/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill while win[] reads Skill/Xerath/Xerath/Xerath/Ahri/Ahri/Ahri.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer exactly, and the whys text describes the same shape (even at 1, Xerath ahead 2-5, Ahri ahead from 6). The full layer was wrong on every row.
audit.corrected: phases[0..6].side rewritten to the content values; ratings realigned to the house scale (5/10 skill, 6/10 Ahri rows, 4/10 Xerath rows).

edits.before: His poke range and passive tankiness let him harass freely without any real risk, a clear lane win for him from here.
edits.after: Eye of Destruction outranges your Q at 1000 to 970, so he harasses free — a clear lane win for him from here.

edits.before: Xerath's Arcanopulse and Eye of Destruction poke you from way outside your Orb range, and his passive mana-shield tankiness lets him spam pokes without needing to trade back.
edits.after: Eye of Destruction (1000) and Shocking Orb (1050) both outrange your 970 Orb, and Mana Surge refills him off every kill, so he pokes without ever needing to trade back.

edits.before: Rite of the Arcane doesn't add engage, and once you have full Spirit Rush mobility you can finally close the distance he's been controlling, flipping the poke war in your favor.
edits.after: Rite of the Arcane immobilizes Xerath for the whole channel and Charm cancels it outright, so once Spirit Rush is online you close the distance he has been controlling and the poke war flips.

edits.before: He becomes a global-siege threat from max range with his ultimate, but if you ever close the gap in a skirmish your burst still deletes his squishy backline before he can kite away.
edits.after: His ultimate sieges from 5000 range, but it roots him in place for the whole channel — flank with Spirit Rush, charm him mid-cast, and the barrage ends with him instead of your team.

edits.before: Level 1 is close since neither side has a meaningful range or rank advantage yet, but from level 2 onward Xerath's range dwarfs your Orb of Deception and his passive shield tankiness means he doesn't even need to play safe while poking you. Play from behind minions, take short trades only when you can guarantee a hit, and prioritize surviving to level 6 with your mana bar intact over trying to win exchanges.
edits.after: Level 1 is close, but from level 2 Eye of Destruction reaches 1000 and Shocking Orb 1050 against your 970 Orb, so he harasses from outside anything you can answer. Mana Surge refunds him off kills, so waiting for him to run dry does not work. Play behind minions, dodge Shocking Orb — 13 seconds at rank 1 — and reach level 6 with health and mana intact instead of chasing exchanges.

edits.before: Level 6 flips the script — once your full Spirit Rush combo is online you finally have the mobility to dash through his poke and land a full burst before he can kite far enough away. His ultimate is a siege tool, not a duel answer, so it doesn't stop your engage. This is where you start punishing every overextension and turning the lane around after surviving the rough early game.
edits.after: Level 6 flips the script — three Spirit Rush dashes cross the zone he has been holding, and he owns no dash to answer with. His ultimate roots him for its whole channel and your Charm cancels it, so it is a siege tool and never a duel answer. Punish every overextension: one dash-in behind a dodged Shocking Orb is his entire health bar.

edits.before: He remains a long-range siege threat in teamfights via his ultimate, capable of poking your whole team from a screen away, so positioning around his ult cooldown matters. But in any skirmish where you actually close the gap on him, your burst combo kills his fragile backline before he can escape — dive him whenever the opportunity opens up rather than trying to out-poke him at range.
edits.after: He stays a long-range siege threat, hitting your team from a screen away, so track the 100-130 second ultimate before you group. But he is rooted while channelling it and has no dash at all — flank with Spirit Rush, charm him mid-cast, and your burst finishes him before the barrage ends. Dive him whenever the angle opens rather than out-poking his range.

edits.before: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb (Stun), denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Xerath wins by landing Shocking Orb into a full artillery rotation and holding you outside 1050 until your health bar is gone.

edits.before: - Xerath Shocking Orb (Stun): matchup-defining — His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Check it before every step-up. - R Spirit Rush (last dash) is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Xerath Shocking Orb: matchup-defining — 13s at rank 1 and his only CC. Dodge it, then step up inside those 13 seconds. - Wait for him to spend Arcanopulse (9s) before you cross the wave. - Charm cancels his ultimate mid-channel, so hold E for the cast, not for poke.

edits.before: Carry through picks — a landed charm is a won fight, and your dashes manufacture charm angles no one wards against.
edits.after: Carry through picks — Xerath owns no dash; one charm inside 975 and he dies where he stands, ultimate or not.

edits.before: If Xerath opens the score, reset expectations and respect Shocking Orb (Stun) doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q clears and stay relevant through charm picks.
edits.after: If Xerath opens the score his poke starts costing you whole waves — farm under tower with Q, dodge Shocking Orb, and take him only when Spirit Rush closes from a flank he has not warded.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt the map: shove with Q, dash-flank every river, and charm-pick Xerath's teammates until the lane lead is a game lead.
edits.after: Ahead, take his range away: shove with Q, then dash-flank other lanes — Xerath alone on a wave is a free charm every time you come back.

edits.before: His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Q out and back through where he stands to last-hit — the return is true damage and he has no shield or dash to blunt it.

edits.before: Q through his last-hit so both hits land, W if he eats the return, and walk — repeat until the charm window is lethal instead of optimistic.
edits.after: Charm his step-up or his ultimate channel — Rite of the Arcane dies on cast and roots him in place while you dash in and finish it.

edits.before: Xerath burns Shocking Orb (Stun) on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Your passive heals at 9 minions — bank it, then step up on his dodged orb.

edits.before: That’s Xerath’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Keep a dash to leave Eye of Destruction's slow zone before the barrage.

edits.before: The last dash is your life insurance — an Ahri who spends all three going in is an assassin's favorite story.
edits.after: A missed charm is 12 seconds spent inside 1050 range with no way to punish him — hold it for his step-up.

edits.before: Charming on cooldown for chip damage and then facing his real engage with nothing — the charm is the matchup, not the poke.
edits.after: With Shocking Orb up he stuns you into a free artillery rotation — check that 13-second cooldown before you cross the wave.

edits.before: Track Xerath’s Shocking Orb (Stun): His only CC — dodge the orb and his artillery never converts into a kill. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Shocking Orb (13s at rank 1): his only CC, and nothing converts without it. Charm also cancels Rite of the Arcane mid-channel.

notes: Two systemic errors fixed: Xerath was described as having 'passive mana-shield tankiness' (Mana Surge is mana restore only, no shield), and the full-layer level chart disagreed with the content layer on all seven rows — full was wrong on every one, content matched packet.levelChart. Chart rows proposed as one atomic group. Charm cancelling Rite of the Arcane was absent from every field and is now in spikes[1], mid, late, dosFull[1] and report[5]. Arcanopulse's charged range is not in the kit file, so no claim was made about it; only W (1000) and E (1050) ranges are cited.
